svg.title: Amazon DynamoDB
svg.desc: Amazon DynamoDB. A serverless key-value and document database: the partition key spreads items across partitions for single-digit-millisecond reads. Step 1, Where it sits: API Gateway → Lambda → PutItem on Orders: no servers to run, and Streams passes each change on. Step 2, Partition and sort key: hash(C-17) picks P2, where orders sit sorted by sort key on 3 replicas. Query: one range. Scan: all. Step 3, Throughput and hot keys: Every guest order uses key GUEST: P3 hits 1,000 writes/s and throttles while P1, P2 idle. Shard it. Step 4, Consistency and limits: byOrderId lags the table, so a lookup misses o-982 briefly. Limits: 400 KB items, keyed queries.

g.text: API Gateway → Lambda → PutItem on Orders: no servers to run, and Streams passes each change on.
hash(C-17) picks P2, where orders sit sorted by sort key on 3 replicas. Query: one range. Scan: all.
Every guest order uses key GUEST: P3 hits 1,000 writes/s and throttles while P1, P2 idle. Shard it.
byOrderId lags the table, so a lookup misses o-982 briefly. Limits: 400 KB items, keyed queries.
partition key customerId · sort key sk = orderDate#orderId
PutItem · hash(partition key) picks the partition
Scan · reads every item in every partition, 1 MB per call
PutItem · hash("GUEST") → P3 · each partition: max 1,000 writes/s
API Gateway → Lambda orders-api → PutItem on table Orders. Each call is a signed HTTPS request: no servers, versions or connection pools.
On-demand capacity: nothing to provision, billed per request. DynamoDB Streams keeps each change for 24 h; order-views updates other views.
Design for access patterns known up front: a customer's orders by customerId, and an order by its number through the GSI byOrderId.
The partition key C-17 is hashed to pick P2; inside it, C-17's items are kept in order of the sort key sk (orderDate#orderId).
P2 lives on 3 replicas in 3 Availability Zones; the write is acknowledged once 2 of the 3 have logged it (USENIX ATC 2022 paper).
A Query with begins_with(sk, "2026-10") reads one range of one partition; a Scan reads every item in the table, 1 MB per call.
Each partition serves at most 3,000 read units and 1,000 write units per second (a write unit is one write of up to 1 KB), in either capacity mode.
Every guest order is saved under GUEST, so 2,400 writes/s land on P3 and it throttles (TableWriteKeyRangeThroughputExceeded).
Adaptive capacity gives a hot partition more of the table's throughput, but never past that limit. Fix the key: an id per guest, or write sharding.
Reads are eventually consistent unless ConsistentRead=true (twice the read units, not on GSIs). byOrderId is updated async, so it missed o-982.
Conditional writes give optimistic locking; a transaction covers up to 100 items. Items are at most 400 KB, and a Query needs the partition key.
No joins or ad hoc queries: export to S3 for analytics. Global tables replicate across Regions: last writer wins, or multi-Region strong consistency.
